analysis.title: Tech sell-off highlights rising scrutiny of AI spending (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: US tech led the market lower on Friday as questions about the AI buildout overshadowed strong 3Q earnings. Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on Friday and 2.0% on the week. S&P 500 fell 1.8% on Friday and 0.6% on the week.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell 1bp on Friday and 7bps on the week to 4.93%. Brent crude rose to USD 118/bbl on Friday on concern the US may resume military strikes against Iran.
On Monday Brent fell more than 4% to below USD 110/bbl as markets focus on extended Iran-Qatar talks. The Kospi rebounded nearly 3% and Nasdaq futures were up 0.9% at the time of writing.

UBS says AI infrastructure demand remains exceptionally strong, but the market debate has shifted. Earnings expectations are broadly being met, and investors now weight overinvestment, financing and cannibalization concerns more heavily.

Overinvestment: Alphabet kept its USD 195-205bn 2026 capex plan, reported negative free cash flow for the quarter and signaled a significant further capex increase for 2027. Its shares fell almost 13% the next day.

Meta raised the lower end of its 2026 capex range to USD 135-145bn and pledged continued aggressive investment beyond this year. Its shares fell nearly 7% the next day on the higher capex floor and negative 3Q free cash flow.

Cloud growth remains strong: Google Cloud revenue rose 103% y/y (82% prior quarter, 34% in the March quarter), Azure grew 48% (43% in the June quarter) and Oracle's cloud growth quickened to 62% from 47%. All three guided to further cloud growth.
Microsoft reported an eight-fold increase in large Copilot accounts and Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users.

Financing: neocloud credit has sold off on a maturity and funding mismatch, with large upfront debt-financed investment supported by later cash flows sensitive to utilization, execution, customer renewal and refinancing.

Neoclouds are about 8% of UBS's capex estimate versus 80% for Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and SpaceX. UBS expects select project delays, repricing and consolidation rather than a broad collapse in AI spending.
Cannibalization: Alphabet Search query growth hit a five-year high but Search revenue growth decelerated, with management saying AI Mode monetizes at a lower rate.

Intel fell 28.6% on Friday. AI is boosting server orders but also causing component scarcity, so Intel could not fully satisfy data center demand, and higher PC prices are hurting its client business.
UBS raised aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027 and introduced USD 1.5tr for 2028.
UBS believes the broader AI trend remains intact but expects higher volatility in the AI trade to be the new normal.

Investment advice: reduce AI overconcentration and diversify across the AI value chain, preferring foundry, compute and power. Rebalance across sectors and asset classes. Preferred equity sectors are industrials, health care and financials. Preferred regions are the Eurozone, emerging markets and Asia ex-Japan. Quality fixed income is favored.
Use volatility deliberately: prepare for further swings and build exposure gradually at predefined prices, rebalance, manage downside risk or generate income.

earnings_insights: Alphabet 3Q (reported, week ended Oct 30): 2026 capex plan maintained at USD 195-205bn, negative free cash flow for the quarter, significant further capex increase signaled for 2027. Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y vs +82% in 2Q and +34% in the March quarter. Search revenue growth decelerated.
Meta 3Q (reported): lower end of 2026 capex range raised to USD 135-145bn, negative free cash flow in 3Q.
Microsoft fiscal 1Q (reported, three months to September): Azure +48% vs +43% for the June quarter. Large Copilot accounts up eight-fold.
Oracle (reported): cloud growth quickened to 62% from 47% in the prior quarter.
Intel (reported): shares fell 28.6% on Friday on data center supply shortfall from component scarcity and PC price headwinds.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell 1bp on Friday and 7bps on the week as quality bonds rallied while stocks fell.
Rose on concern the US may resume strikes on Iran, then fell more than 4% on Monday as Iran-Qatar talks were extended.
Raised forecasts reflect stronger commitments from the largest hyperscalers.

risk_factors: AI lab revenue growth slowing meaningfully.
Falling AI costs failing to stimulate enough new usage to absorb expanding capacity.
Algorithmic efficiency gains sharply reducing compute requirements.
Large investments failing to deliver commensurate improvements in AI capabilities.
Significant deterioration in financial conditions constraining hyperscalers' willingness to fund new investment.
Neocloud maturity and funding mismatch, with project delays, repricing and consolidation likely.
Single-stock risk is elevated this earnings season.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects higher volatility in the AI trade to be the new normal at this stage of the cycle.

Investors should prepare for further volatility, decide in advance how to respond, and consider building exposure gradually at predefined prices or generating income. Structured strategies carry issuer, liquidity, pricing and capital-loss risks.
geopolitical: Concern that the US may resume military strikes against Iran pushed Brent to USD 118/bbl on Friday.
Extended Iran-Qatar talks helped Brent fall more than 4% to below USD 110/bbl on Monday.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth is accelerating (Google Cloud +103%, Azure +48%, Oracle +62%), advance orders for compute are expanding, and UBS raised its AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Alphabet and Meta posted negative 3Q free cash flow with higher capex ahead, neocloud credit sold off on funding mismatch, and Alphabet Search monetization is under pressure from AI Mode.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS would be concerned if AI lab revenue growth slows meaningfully, cloud utilization weakens, or falling AI costs fail to stimulate enough new usage to absorb expanding capacity.
